class: Suggested jobs could not be fetched by country: no job carried a normalized country, so the only country rule was a score-time exclusion and there was no way to ask for one country's jobs
fix: New geo_reference.location_countries (each listed place read as a country first, then as a US state, so 'Austin, TX' is US and 'Georgia' stays the country) and primary_country (the owner's country when named, the only country named, else unknown, never guessed). discovered_jobs gains country_code, stamped on every scan and backfilled for old rows; get_discovered_jobs takes country_code and the Suggested jobs page passes ?country= (upper-cased, two letters, anything else ignored). job_discovery._in_reach now uses the same parser, so scoring and fetching agree.
prevention: A filter the owner can ask for is stored on the row at ingest, backfilled for old rows, and parsed by one shared function that scoring also uses -- never re-derived per call site.
root_cause: The scan stored each job's location as a raw string and applied the country only as a score-time veto (_in_reach): a US-state spelling was not recognised as the US at all, nothing was stored per job, and neither the engine nor the page offered a country filter.
site: job_discovery.py, geo_reference.py and the Suggested jobs page of web_ui.py, 3 November 2026
symptom: The owner asked to fetch jobs based on the country. The scan kept no country per job, 'Austin, TX' was not known to be a US location, and there was no way to ask for one country's suggestions.
why_tests_missed: Discovery tests checked scoring, ordering and freshness, but no test asked what country a stored job was in or whether one country's jobs could be fetched; the country rule was only exercised as a veto inside the score.
